/assets/ping/media/6954e47a9ac533d993ab9.title: Ping

blocks.text: Ping is a voice messaging device that keeps families connected without smartphone distractions. No browsing capabilities, no buzzing alerts. Just simple communication that lets kids stay focused on being kids.
Developed in Spring 2025 at MIT on a seven-person team of MBAs, engineers, and a UI/UX designer.

/assets/ping/media/6954e5cc05ce517d28b32.alt: Children running outdoors beside a statement about connected devices.

blocks.text: Technology lets families stay connected when it matters, but the devices kids use are often loaded with features that distract from growing up.

/assets/ping/media/6954e5dcd0ebbca07d234.alt: Three research columns with photographs of families and children using devices.
/assets/ping/media/6954e5dcd0ebbca07d234.heading: Why do families give their kids mobile devices?

blocks.heading: Families want to stay connected
blocks.text: Parents need reliable ways to reach their children and ensure their safety during emergencies. Mobile devices provide this essential connection.

blocks.heading: Smart devices solve parents worries
blocks.text: Modern devices include safety tools, location sharing, and communication features that address parents' core concerns about their children's wellbeing.

blocks.heading: Parent anxiety outweighs device misuse concerns
blocks.text: Parents know smart devices expose kids to apps, distractions, and online risks. But the fear of being unable to reach their child is more tangible, justifying a trade-off.

/assets/ping/media/6954e5fe529845a0d1d14.alt: Comparison chart for phones, smartwatches and trackers with green and red markers.
/assets/ping/media/6954e5fe529845a0d1d14.heading: Current options trade capability for distraction and control.

blocks.heading: Phones
list: Device that does everything: calls, texts, apps, camera, GPS, tracking
Distraction of full internet and attention traps in a Childs pocket
Safety controls are bolted on adult settings, easy to misconfigure or bypass

blocks.heading: Smartwatches
list: Communication and tracking with fewer distractions than a phone
Phone behavior on wrist, calls, texts, notifications urgently grab attention
Short battery life of one day relies on frequent charging habits
Kid branded watches can feel babyish or like a ‘my parents do not trust me’ badge, so kids hide them or do not want to wear them

blocks.heading: Trackers
list: Surveillance first tool that treat kids like objects and only assure parents
No way to communicate through the tag, so families still need another device for communication

/assets/ping/media/6954e60420f0839d3a9c0.alt: A blurred photograph of a child running outdoors behind the design question.

blocks.text: How might we create a device that keeps families connected when it matters, while keeping the internet's distractions out?

/assets/ping/media/69571cc2cda1499b34d96.alt: A black Ping device worn on a wrist with a heart on its screen.

/assets/ping/media/6954e60bd993fd9b12f66.alt: A Ping pendant clipped to a patterned jacket zipper.

blocks.text: Ping is a communication device for kids that lets them exchange voice messages and location with their families.

/assets/ping/media/6954e6105c2847a6ec297.alt: Diagram connecting a Ping device to a parent's phone, with other communications outside the loop.

blocks.text: Ping operates within a closed loop system, keeping the distractions of the internet out

/assets/ping/media/6954e6134a140b3b2417e.alt: Red, black and green Ping devices showing buttons and screens.

blocks.text: Ping interface focuses on the essentials: front buttons for voice messaging, side navigation buttons for selecting contacts, and an emergency button

/assets/ping/media/ping-functions.mp4.alt: Animation demonstrating the Ping device's buttons and screen.

/assets/ping/media/12.mp4.alt: Animation showing a Ping device beside the parent's phone interface.

blocks.text: The parents companion app shows information only when parents actively request it, making every check-in a deliberate choice rather than passive surveillance.

/assets/ping/media/app-functions.mp4.alt: Three phone screens demonstrating messaging, location and emergency actions.
/assets/ping/media/app-functions.mp4.heading: App functionality

blocks.heading: Messaging
blocks.text: Easily send and receive pings from your kid, or review past messages.

blocks.heading: Location
blocks.text: Location is revealed progressively, encouraging parents to monitor responsibly rather than habitually track.

blocks.heading: Emergencies
blocks.text: In an emergency, parents get specific actions to defuse or escalate as needed.

/assets/ping/media/695ed81af0021571e8551.alt: Blue and red Ping pendants and a green wrist strap with different screen designs.

blocks.text: Accessories come in varied colors, forms, and collabs, so younger kids can show off a Bluey necklace or Minecraft watch, while older kids can opt for simpler mature styles.
